chunks: And the Sheikh — may Allah support him — informed me, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn al-Hasan, from his father, from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa and al-Husayn ibn al-Hasan ibn Aban — both together — from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Safwan, from Ishaq ibn Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him):

He said: I asked him about madhy. He said: «Indeed, Ali (peace be upon him) was a man who produced much madhy, and he was too modest to ask the Messenger of Allah — may Allah bless him and his family — because of [his relationship with] Fatimah (peace be upon her). So he commanded al-Miqdad to ask him while he was seated. Al-Miqdad asked him, and he said to him: «It is nothing.»»

key_terms.الْمَذْيِ: madhy — pre-seminal (Cowper's gland) fluid emitted without ejaculatory sensation; the legal question is whether it necessitates ghusl
key_terms.لَيْسَ بِشَيْءٍ: it is nothing — a formulaic Prophetic legal declaration that the substance carries no ritual consequence (no ghusl, no najasah in Shia fiqh)
key_terms.لِمَكَانِ: because of the position/relationship of — out of regard for Fatimah's bond to the Prophet as his daughter and Ali's wife
key_terms.مَذَّاءً: one who frequently and copiously produces madhy (intensive form)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on madhy (pre-seminal fluid) according to Imam al-Sadiq (AS) in Tahdhib al-Ahkam, and why did Imam Ali send al-Miqdad to ask the Prophet?
ai.summary: Ishaq ibn Ammar asked Imam al-Sadiq (AS) about the legal ruling on madhy (pre-seminal fluid). The Imam answered with the well-known precedent: Imam Ali (AS), who frequently emitted madhy, was too modest to ask the Prophet (SAWW) about it directly out of regard for his wife Fatimah (AS)—the Prophet's own daughter—and so deputised al-Miqdad ibn al-Aswad to pose the question on his behalf while the Prophet was seated in a gathering. The Prophet's ruling was terse and decisive: 'It is nothing,' establishing in Shia fiqh that madhy is tahir and carries no obligation of ghusl.
